newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Reuters poll puts Taiwan Q1 growth at 6.48 pct.
newsitem.headline: Reuters poll puts Taiwan Q1 growth at 6.48 pct.

text.p: A Reuters Poll of Taiwan economists projects year-on-year gross domestic product growth of 6.48 percent in the first quarter of 1997, above the government's own recent forecast.
Official first-quarter GDP figures were to be released by the Directorate General of Budget, Accounting and Statistics at about 0820 GMT on May 16.
GDP rose a year-on-year 6.62 percent in the fourth quarter of 1996.
The average 6.48 percent forecast was higher than the statistics directorate's February forecast of 6.40 percent.
A directorate official had said in late April that first-quarter GDP would likely rise around 6.6 percent due to improved exports, imports and industrial output performance.
Economists cautioned that the directorate's February forecast for government investment growth was over-optimistic.

"The directorate forecast in February that first-quarter government investment would grow 4.81 percent year-on-year, reversing a 4.08 percent decline in the fourth quarter, but I doubt it," said Nomura Securities economist Amy Huang.
"Indeed the government has accelerated public construction recently, but whether growth is so significant remains to be seen," Huang said.

Grand Cathay Securities vice-president Terry Chen said she had boosted her GDP forecast because private consumption in the first quarter -- fuelled by a rallying stock market -- was likely to have risen significantly.
The stock index had risen more than 20 percent alone in the first quarter.
